reviewVerdicts.rationale: Question 1: No. The required procedure mandates manifest-order, one-file-per-command rereads (workspace/.agents/skills/review/SKILL.md:50-56). The purported final 92-file manifest is recorded at backend-review.log:9843, but its reread repeats docs/analysis/03-functional-requirements.md at backend-review.log:10069 after all five requirements and before config, and repeats TodoAuthController.ts at backend-review.log:10232 after executable/schema.ts and before executable/server.ts. Thus the claimed final dry round (backend-review.log:10606-10659 and 11192-11500) was not a valid ordered round. Question 2: No. The testing instructions require observable follow-up proof for persisted mutations and raw HTTP for malformed payloads, prohibit casts, and require concrete refusal assertions (workspace/.agents/skills/backend/testing.md:132-162, 166-174). The tests send invalid typed-SDK inputs via `as never` and accept any thrown error in `test_api_todo_todo_content_boundaries.ts:19-29, 42-47, 61-68` and `test_api_todo_boundary_state.ts:75-106`; creation only checks the response with no follow-up observation in `test_api_todo_todo_create.ts:20-29`. The stream's runtime pass claims were not independently rerun and are unverified, but do not affect these failures.

These cited facts are verified; the required watcher gate is unverified.

The watcher being merely reported active at :4893 and :5461 is not proof of a clean rebuild; that gate is unverified. Question 2: pass. The testing instructions require one primary operation and a business assertion (.agents/skills/backend/testing.md:34-42,158). The suite covers all 24 accessors (workspace operation inventory; stream :4893-4946), and tests assert outcomes: creation checks persisted detail and empty history (packages/backend/test/features/api/todo/todo/test_api_todo_todo_create.ts:27-59), browsing checks filters, ordering, and pagination (test_api_todo_todo_index.ts:39-99), stale edits check preserved content and history (test_api_todo_todo_update_stale.ts:28-50), and refusal helpers assert client/error status (packages/backend/test/helpers/TodoTestUtil.ts:35-63).

These are verified from the final workspace files. I did not independently execute the tests or live application; those runtime results are unverified.

The tests are also not properly written: frontend verification requires observable success/refusal assertions in the journeys run in both simulation and live modes (.agents/skills/frontend/verification.md:24-53, 68-79, 109-118), but business assertions are guarded by runWhenLive in auth-provision.spec.ts:5-22, auth-security.spec.ts:5-31, profile-security.spec.ts:10-88, todo-workflow.spec.ts:5-79, and trash-recovery.spec.ts:5-52; the edge-case refusal tests are entirely no-ops under simulation (edge-cases.spec.ts:19-128). Thus simulation passes can prove only navigation/reachability for those promised behaviors. I did not independently rerun the reported tests; the stream's pass claims are therefore unverified independently.
